title: App Statistic reads JoomlArt as the account source of a first sign-in through JoomlArt, and Tracy answers /favicon.ico with its own icon instead of treating it as a site address
steps: Run the App Statistic backend test that signs four accounts in through the real PostgreSQL identity store: JoomlArt with no utm, JoomlArt with utm medium and campaign but no utm_source, JoomlArt with utm_source newsletter, and Google.
Run the favicon tests: GET /favicon.ico on Tracy's own hostname signed out and signed in, GET /favicon.ico on a site hostname, and read packages/web/tracy-harness/index.html and public/favicon.svg.
expect: The JoomlArt account with no utm reads source {source: joomlart} in users, quickstarts and detail; the source filter joomlart lists it and the source options include joomlart.
A JoomlArt account whose link carried utm medium/campaign keeps them and gains source joomlart; one whose link named utm_source newsletter keeps newsletter.
A Google first sign-in with no utm stays unknown (source null): a way to sign in is not an acquisition source.
GET /favicon.ico on Tracy's hostname answers 200 image/svg+xml with exactly the icon page-shell pages declare, signed out and signed in (before: 302 to /login or to /favicon-ico-…/join).
GET /favicon.ico on a site hostname is not answered with Tracy's icon.
The /ops bundle's index.html declares <link rel=icon type=image/svg+xml href=/favicon.svg> and its public/favicon.svg equals that icon byte for byte.
fence: Read-side only for the source: account_source derives joomlart from the first sign-in's recorded via, never from a later identity link; /favicon.ico is registered after customer-site host routing.

tests: an account whose first sign-in came through JoomlArt sign-in reads JoomlArt as its source
/favicon.ico on Tracy's own hostname is Tracy's icon, never a site address
the /ops bundle declares the same Tracy icon, so the browser never asks for /favicon.ico
